🔻 US bases in region suffered serious damage: Iran Army spokesperson

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Mohammad Akrami-Nia says US bases in the region have suffered serious damage, noting that the damage has affected the support and supply operations of American forces and created challenges for Washington.

Brigadier General Akrami-Nia made the remarks in response to the al-Alam correspondent’s questions about US movements in the region, the possibility of war, the Strait of Hormuz, and long-term war.
​
Referring to US movements and deployments in the region, the Army spokesperson said Iran’s Armed Forces had used the ceasefire period to update their target bank, optimize existing equipment, introduce new equipment into their military structure, and draw on the experiences and lessons learned from the war. He said the aim was to ensure that, in the event of another attack or aggression, Iran could confront the enemy more effectively, forcefully and on an even broader scale than before.
​
He said US bases in the region had suffered serious damage, adding that aerial, satellite and field observations confirmed this. He added that available information indicated that most of the bases were no longer even repairable.
​
Akrami-Nia added that the damage to US bases in the region had created serious problems for the support, fuel and food supplies of American forces, forcing the United States to obtain its supplies from outside the region.
​
He also said US soldiers were facing psychological problems and that Washington might take action to change the situation. He said the United States had lacked a clear strategy for withdrawing from the war from the outset and had become confused after witnessing the resistance of Iran’s Armed Forces and the support of the Iranian people.
​
Akrami-Nia said contradictory statements by the US officials about the ceasefire, continuation of the war, a naval blockade and the Strait of Hormuz showed that Washington lacked a clear strategy for ending the war, adding that the United States could take unpredictable actions.
​
Tehran’s preemptive operations based on proportional response to imminent threats
​
Brigadier General Akrami-Nia discussed Iran’s military strategy following the 12-day war, saying that under the UN Charter, the use of force is prohibited except in cases of legitimate self-defense, and that Iran had shifted its strategy toward preemptive warfare.
​
The Army spokesperson said the principles of proportionality, immediacy and necessity had been observed in Iran’s preemptive operations. He said responses had been proportionate to the threat, operations had not been expanded beyond that, and preemptive operations had only been conducted when necessary and when there was an imminent threat.
​
He added that if Iran concludes in the future that the enemy is preparing an imminent attack, it will carry out a preemptive operation.
​
US prioritizes Israel’s security over regional countries’ interests
​
Akrami-Nia said the United States did not prioritize the security and national interests of regional countries and instead pursued Israel’s security. He described regional countries as Iran’s friends and brothers and Israel as a common enemy.
​
He added that the United States had sought through divisive policies to divert the region’s attention from the threat posed by Zionism.
​
Akrami-Nia also said Iran had not targeted the people or infrastructure of regional countries during the recent war and had instead targeted US bases.

📄 Israel puts senior Hamas leaders abroad on assassination target list

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Israel has placed senior Hamas leaders living outside the Gaza Strip on a list of assassination targets, Israeli minister in charge of military affairs said, according to Al Arabiya.

Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Israel had put a plan to target Hamas leaders outside the occupied territories on its agenda.
​
The move follows earlier Israeli statements indicating that operations against Hamas leaders would not be limited to the Gaza Strip. Israeli military chief Eyal Zamir said in September 2025 that the scope of targeting Hamas commanders would extend beyond Gaza.
​
Several prominent Hamas figures are based outside Gaza, including Khalil al-Hayya, the group’s political bureau chief, Khaled Meshaal, Musa Abu Marzouk and Osama Hamdan.
​
Israel has previously targeted senior Hamas figures outside Gaza. Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh was killed in Tehran in July 2024, while senior Hamas official Saleh al-Arouri was killed in Beirut in January 2024.
